speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual start; could you please describe your specific medical history and any prior diagnoses? Have you noticed any recent changes in your vision or hearing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; does this ataxia come on suddenly after a specific event, or has it progressed gradually over weeks? Additionally, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, or any issues with your speech and coordination? Please describe your full medical history, specifically any history of strokes, multiple sclerosis, or autoimmune conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab and symptoms of acute ataxia, I suspect Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain Axial and Coronal views. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).
